newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: China believes Yeltsin has Parkinson's - report.
newsitem.headline: China believes Yeltsin has Parkinson's - report.

text.p: An Australian newspaper on Friday reported that Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng believed Russian President Boris Yeltsin had Parkinson's disease after meeting him last December.
The Sydney Morning Herald reported a leaked Australian foreign affairs document saying Li "mimicked" Yeltsin's condition after meeting him in Moscow.
The document said Li told his ambassador to Russia: "Ambassador, this is Parkinson's disease".

An Australian foreign affairs spokesman would not confirm the veracity of the document. "We don't comment on supposed leaks," he said. The newspaper said the Australian foreign affairs document was a cable from Australia's ambassador to Moscow, Geoff Bentley, headed "Yeltsin's health: Li Peng's diagnosis".
Bentley reportedly said Yeltsin's health was discussed at length at a recent meeting of Asian ambassadors he attended.
Bentley said the Chinese ambassador "recounted how Yeltsin's jaw had been shaky" during his meeting with Li.
"Coming away from the meeting Li Peng mimicked Yeltsin's condition and commented: 'Ambassador, this is Parkinson's disease'," Bentley said.
Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, who died last month, was in the advanced stages of Parkinson's disease.
Spectulation over 66-year-old Yeltsin's health has been rife in recent months, following heart surgery and a bout of pneumonia.
